name: 110 (One Hundred and Ten)
description: 110 (One Hundred and Ten) is an Irish trick-taking game with bidding, related to Twenty-Five. Played with a standard 52-card deck; the first player or team to reach 110 points wins. Players score 5 points per trick. Card ranking varies by trump suit.

content.text: 110 (One Hundred and Ten) is an Irish trick-taking game with bidding, related to Twenty-Five. Played with a standard 52-card deck; the first player or team to reach 110 points wins. Players score 5 points per trick. Card ranking varies by trump suit.
Ireland. Bidding version of the game Twenty-Five; part of the Irish trick-taking family (Twenty-Five, 55, 110, 220).
2–9 (five cards each plus five-card kitty from one 52-card pack)
Five cards to each player and five to the kitty (two then three or three then two at a time); deal passes left.

items.text: Only bidder can win: Some groups play that only the bidder can win the game; if someone reaches 110 points through tricks taken against another player's bid, the game continues until the bidder wins or loses.
Bidder names trump before kitty: In some circles the bidder must name the trump suit before looking at the five-card kitty instead of naming trump after picking up and discarding.
Different first lead: Some play that the first lead comes from the player to the left of the bidder; others play that the player to the right of the bidder leads the first trick instead.
Bidder scores only bid amount: Some groups rule that the bidder can only score the amount bid; for example, a bid of 15 that wins all five tricks still scores 15 rather than 30.
